## Electronic timing guide (SPORTident and EasyGecNG)

The full text of the site's Electronic Timing pages. Use it when someone asks about electronic timing, SPORTident, SI boxes, SI cards or EasyGecNG. For a problem, walk them through the Troubleshooting fixes one step at a time, in the order given, asking what they see after each step; don't list every fix at once. If SI cards don't read, start with trying each COM port in the COM Port menu, which is the most common fix. If a student gets a sad face, the most likely reason is that they really skipped a checkpoint, went out of order, or didn't hold the SI card in a box until it beeped: first have them run the course again with a reminder of how. Only if students who clearly did the course right keep getting sad faces, check box placement and then synchronize the boxes. Link the relevant page. Don't invent steps, menu names or settings that are not in this guide; if the guide doesn't cover the problem, suggest they email admin@navigationgames.org with a photo of the screen.

## Electronic Timing

Navigation Games often uses an electronic timing system with its orienteering activities. You do not need electronics to teach orienteering! Every lesson in this curriculum works without it. We use it because it helps us make sure students understand the activity, because kids love the beeping, and because it frees us from checking results so we can focus on teaching.

The timing system does two jobs:

1. **Checking** that each student visited all the checkpoints in the right order
2. **Timing** how long the course took

Both can be done without electronics. Students can check themselves by matching a picture or code at each checkpoint to their clue sheet, or a partner can check them (see [Checking](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/frameworks/skill-concept-sequence/#checking) and [Checkpoints](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/controls-and-punches)). A stopwatch or a class timer handles the timing.

### SPORTident and EasyGecNG

[SPORTident](https://www.sportident.com/) is the electronic timing system used at most orienteering events around the world. Each student carries an **SI card**, and each checkpoint has an **SI box**. Students check in by putting the SI card into the hole in the box. The box beeps and flashes and the card records the visit.

**EasyGecNG** is the program that reads the SI cards at the end of a course. It tells each student whether they visited the checkpoints in the right order and shows their time. A smiley face means the course was done correctly. Navigation Games made EasyGecNG from EasyGec, a program by Thierry Porret, to give students easier-to-read feedback about which checkpoints they missed. Intern Charlie Moore [wrote about why we changed it](https://www.navigationgames.org/post/in-the-works-new-software-for-teaching-orienteering). Huge thanks to T. Porret for sharing his code and letting us distribute it as open source.

### What students do

1. **Clear.** Check in at the Clear box. This erases the SI card from the last run.
2. **Start.** Check in at the Start box. The time starts.
3. **Checkpoints.** Visit each checkpoint in order and check in at its SI box. Hold the SI card in the box until it beeps.
4. **Finish.** Check in at the Finish box. The time stops.
5. **Download.** Put the SI card in the mini reader at the computer. EasyGecNG shows whether you got it right, and your time.

If a box doesn't beep, the card probably wasn't cleared. Go back to the Clear box.

### Timing individuals and timing the whole class

Orienteering is normally a timed sport, like cross country running or skiing. Timing students is a great way to encourage them to build speed, improve their skills and even practice their memory, as in Animal-O, where students repeat a course faster and then from memory. It also gives competition to students who want it. Not every student is comfortable being timed, though, especially while they're still learning a new activity. Even when you time students, emphasize accuracy over raw speed. Finding all the right checkpoints matters more than finding them quickly.

You can also time the whole class against one clock. This unites the students and builds teamwork. It sets the expectation that everyone is working together and that each person's actions affect the group, and it encourages students to help each other learn.

## Equipment for Electronic Timing

To build one complete set for teaching orienteering with electronic timing, schools buy:

- **SPORTident school kit** from [sportident.us](https://www.sportident.us/product-page/school-and-training-set), and 13 [mounting holders](https://www.sportident.us/product-page/mounting-holder) that fit the SI boxes in the kit. The kit cost about $2,800 in August 2025 and has gone up since because of tariffs. SPORTident USA can take a credit card or give you a quote so you can raise a purchase order. They ship the kit with an invoice. If kits are out of stock, the whole process can take 4 to 6 weeks.
- **13 traffic cones with holes in the top.** We recommend 12-inch cones ([example](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C7SR23YR)) because they're easier to carry. 18-inch cones ([example](https://www.amazon.com/Traffic-Collars-Parking-Control-Construction/dp/B0CPP3NFBT/)) are sturdier but harder to carry.
- **A hardwood dowel** that fits into the top of the cones, and screws to attach the mounting holders (see [Cone toppers](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/equipment/#cone-toppers) below).
- **A Windows computer or tablet** to run EasyGecNG. Pick one with good battery life for use outdoors. See [Installing EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/installing/).
- **A [Navigation Games kit](https://www.navigationgames.org/product-page/beginning-orienteering-instruction-kit)** with the laminated materials (animal pictures, clue sheets, maps). See [Navigation Games Kits](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/kits).

### What's in the SPORTident school kit

- **SI boxes** numbered 31 to 40 for the checkpoints, plus Start, Finish and Clear boxes. The Clear box is also the **SI-Master**, used to synchronize the other boxes' clocks (see [Maintaining the SI Boxes](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/)).
- **A mini reader** (also called the download box) that plugs into the computer's USB port and reads the SI cards.
- **30 SI cards** and 30 Velcro strips to attach to them.

Maintenance also uses a coupling stick and a Service/OFF card (see [Maintaining the SI Boxes](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/)).

### Putting it together

1. Make the cone toppers with the dowels, screws and mounting holders.
2. Attach the Velcro strips to the SI cards.
3. Install the software on the computer ([Installing EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/installing/)).

### Cone toppers

Navigation Games uses cone toppers to hold SI boxes on traffic cones, indoors and outdoors.

1. Cut a wooden dowel into 3-inch lengths. Use a hardwood like oak or maple, not pine, so the screws hold better in the end grain. The dowel should fit snugly into the top of your cones without being hard to push in.
2. Screw the black SI box mounting holders into the ends of the dowels. SPORTident USA sells the holders. Their website may not show everything they offer, so contact them if you don't see it.

Navigation Games can make the cone toppers for you. [Contact us](mailto:admin@navigationgames.org) for a quote.

### You might also want

- An Android phone or tablet with SPORTident's apps, to read SI cards and print results without a Windows computer. This matters less for elementary school PE than running EasyGecNG.
- Other orienteering supplies from [Berman's O Supply](https://bermansosupply.com/) or [The Compass Store](https://www.thecompassstore.com/).

## Installing EasyGecNG

EasyGecNG runs on Windows. It can also run on Mac and Linux; the [EasyGecNG page on GitHub](https://github.com/Navigation-Games/EasyGecNG) explains how. EasyGecNG is a Java program, and its source code is public if your IT department wants to review it.

### 1. Install the SPORTident USB driver

Download the USB driver from [SPORTident's software page](https://www.sportident.com/products.html#software) and install it. You may also need to install the Microsoft .NET framework. Restart the computer after installing the driver.

### 2. Install Java 8

EasyGecNG needs Java 8. We use version 8u231. Get it from [Oracle's Java 8 archive](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/javase8u211-later-archive-downloads.html) (search the page for "8u231").

Then turn off automatic Java updates, because EasyGecNG needs this older version:

1. Open the Windows Control Panel and search for **Java**. Open the Java Control Panel.
2. On the **Update** tab, uncheck **Check for Updates Automatically**.
3. In the window that pops up, click **Do Not Check**, then **OK**.

### 3. Download EasyGecNG

1. Go to [github.com/Navigation-Games/EasyGecNG](https://github.com/Navigation-Games/EasyGecNG).
2. On the right side of the page, under **Releases**, click the release marked with a green **Latest** label. (Or go straight to the [releases page](https://github.com/Navigation-Games/EasyGecNG/releases) and find the one marked **Latest**.) Skip the releases named "alpha"; those are test builds.
3. Under **Assets** at the bottom of that release, click the `.zip` file (for example, `EasyGecNG-v1.1.2.zip`) to download it.
4. Unzip it: in File Explorer, right-click the downloaded file, choose **Extract All...**, and extract it to a folder you'll remember.

The unzipped folder has `bin`, `doc` and `lib` folders inside it.

### 4. Start EasyGecNG

Open the `bin` folder and double-click **EasyGecNG**, the one whose type is "Windows Batch File". (There's another file with the same name and no extension. That one is for Mac and Linux.)

To make it easier to find in class, right-click that file and choose **Send to > Desktop (create shortcut)**.

### 5. Test it

Plug the mini reader into a USB port. It beeps twice. Start EasyGecNG and check that it reads an SI card (see [Running EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/), steps 4 and 8 to 10). Then confirm that you can save results.

If EasyGecNG doesn't read the card, the usual fix is to choose a different COM port. See [Troubleshooting](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/troubleshooting/).

### 6. Get the course files

Download the clean course files for your animal set (see [Clean course files](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#clean-course-files)) and put them in a folder on the Desktop, such as `Orienteering Courses`.

### Other software

These are useful but not needed to run classes:

- **[SPORTident Config+](https://www.sportident.com/products.html#software)**: for maintaining the SI boxes (checking batteries, synchronizing clocks, changing box numbers). See [Maintaining the SI Boxes](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/).
- **[Purple Pen](https://purplepen.golde.org/)**: for drawing courses on a map.
- **[OpenOrienteering Mapper](https://www.openorienteering.org/apps/mapper/)**: for drawing or updating a map.
- **[EasyGec](http://t.porret.free.fr/lienlogiciel.php?idmenu=60)**: the original program by Thierry Porret (website in French), as a backup if EasyGecNG has a problem. Download it from the "Télécharger" button.

## Running EasyGecNG

Before class:

- **Charge the laptop** between classes.
- **Print this page and keep it with the computer** during class.
- **Know your school's IT help desk number.**

### What you need

- SI boxes: checkpoints 31 to 40, Clear, Start and Finish
- The mini reader (download box), with its USB cord
- SI cards
- A laptop with EasyGecNG installed ([Installing EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/installing/))
- A course file (`.egc`) with the courses already built. See [Clean course files](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#clean-course-files).

### Steps

1. **Sign in to the laptop.**

2. **Connect the mini reader.** Plug it into a USB port. It beeps twice.

3. **Start EasyGecNG.** Double-click the EasyGecNG shortcut on the Desktop, or open the EasyGecNG folder, then `bin`, and double-click **EasyGecNG** (Windows Batch File).

4. **Check the COM port.** Under "Reading Si-card", look at the **COM Port** menu. If it's blank, click it and choose a port. If there are no choices, check that the mini reader is plugged in, then click the blue and white arrow next to the menu to look again. If the computer shows more than one COM port, you may need to try each one until cards read (step 10).

5. **Open the course file.** Click the **Open** icon (under File, the second icon) and open the Animal-O `.egc` file for your school, usually in a Desktop folder such as `Orienteering Courses`. If EasyGecNG asks "Do you want to save the current event?", click **No**.

6. **Check the output mode.** Results should show as a smiley face (pass) or a sad face (mistake). Newer versions start this way. If results show as a table, click the **Parameters** icon to switch to face view (see [Tabular view](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#tabular-view)).

7. **Set the display time.** Click the tools icon under Parameters to set how many seconds each result stays on the screen. We like 2 seconds (the minimum) so students can download quickly one after another. When students are just starting, or to help them understand a mistake, set it longer.

8. **Click the green Start button** (next to "Zero time"). The button turns orange, then red, and the mini reader beeps twice. EasyGecNG is now ready to read cards. The red button is the Stop button.

9. **Try a course yourself before the students do.** Take an SI card and check in at the boxes in order: Clear, Start, the checkpoints on one of your courses, then Finish. That is super important. The best time is before you set the checkpoints out, with the boxes side by side, so only a second or two passes between check-ins. If a box's clock has drifted, even a little, a quick course like this shows it: you get a sad face for a course you did right. Then [synchronize the boxes](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/#synchronizing-the-si-boxes) before class.

10. **Download the SI card.** Put the card in the mini reader. The reader beeps once, and the computer shows the result and plays a sound. If nothing happens, see [Troubleshooting](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/troubleshooting/). The most common fix is choosing a different COM port.

11. **When you're done**, close EasyGecNG with the X at the top right. When it asks "Do you want to save the current event?", click **No** unless you want to keep the results.

### Practice scenarios

Before class, repeat steps 9 and 10 to see what EasyGecNG shows when:

- You mispunch (skip a checkpoint or visit them out of order)
- You forget to check in at the Clear box before the course
- You forget to check in at the Start box
- You forget to check in at the Finish box

You don't need to save the file after class unless you want to look at the results later.

### Tabular view

If a student makes a mistake and you have time, switch to tabular view and have them download again to see which checkpoints they visited. Tabular view also lets you fix it when EasyGecNG guesses the wrong course for a student: change the course by hand.

Click the **Parameters** icon to switch between face view and tabular view. In face view the icon shows a table; in tabular view it shows a smiley face. Switch back to face view afterward.

### Clean course files

EasyGecNG saves everything in files ending in `.egc`:

- **Courses**: the sequence of checkpoint codes for each course
- **Orienteers**: each SI card number, and the student's name if you entered it
- **Results**: the checkpoints each student visited on each course, and their time

Each time you save, all the results are saved in the file. If you use the same file for many classes, the results pile up and the file gets big and slow. Start fresh with a clean copy from time to time.

Download clean course files for the animals in your kit:

- **[Classic animals](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RFKnIUBX-Wkrju4UiEa98A7pknrj8b0J?usp=drive_link)**
- **[Carlson animals](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1eWLyyZ4q5q-jDUCuoQuPK9-0AL8Y3uYU?usp=drive_link)**

To make a fresh copy on the laptop:

1. Open the `Orienteering Courses` folder on the Desktop.
2. Make a new folder for the copy.
3. Open the `Clean - copy from here` folder, copy `Animal-O_30s_and_40s.egc` (Ctrl-C), and paste it into your new folder (Ctrl-V).

If EasyGecNG then can't save the file (the message may be in French and mention a "fichier"), fix the folder's permissions. See "Access denied" in [Troubleshooting](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/troubleshooting/#access-denied-or-cant-save-the-file).

### Assigning SI cards to students

When you assign SI cards to students, you can see each student's results by name, and if a card is missing at the end of class, you know whose it is. EasyGecNG shows each student by SI card number until you assign names.

**One at a time:** click the green and white **+** next to the Orienteers box. Type the last name, first name and SI card number, then click **Validate**.

**From a file:** make a text file in Notepad with one line per student: SI card number, last name and first name, separated by semicolons. Choose **Save As**, set the file type to **All files**, and end the file name in `.csv`. Then import it with the icon above the green **+** next to the Orienteers box. For example:

```
2301250;P;Charlie
2301246;B;Barb
2301253;P;Maija
```

### Create a new event and course

1. Click the pencil icon under **File** to start a new event.
2. Click the green and white **+** next to the Courses box and name the course.
3. Click the green and white **+** next to the Codes box and choose the checkpoint codes for the course, in order.
4. Test it by doing the course with an SI card and downloading it.

### Mass-start Score-O

In a Score-O, students visit the checkpoints in any order. EasyGecNG can check whether they got them all and report how many they visited.

In a mass start, everyone starts at the same time and doesn't check in at the Start box. They still need to check in at the Clear box first.

Set up a new course as above, but choose **Mass start** under "Type of Start" and **Score Race** under "Type of course". Enter the time of the mass start. Getting the time right may take some fiddling: download an SI card in tabular view to see EasyGecNG's idea of the current time, and compare it to your watch.

## Troubleshooting Electronic Timing

Problems are listed by what you see. Try the fixes in order.

### EasyGecNG doesn't read SI cards

You put an SI card in the mini reader and nothing shows on the screen, or the mini reader doesn't beep.

1. **Try a different COM port.** This is the most common fix. Under "Reading Si-card", click the **COM Port** menu. If there is more than one port (for example COM3 and COM4), you have to find the one the mini reader is using. Click the red Stop button, choose another port, click the green Start button, and download a card again. Try each port in the list until a card reads.

2. **If the COM Port menu is blank**, check that the mini reader is plugged in, then click the blue and white arrow next to the menu to look again. Unplug the mini reader and plug it back in. It should beep twice.

3. **Check that EasyGecNG is reading.** The button next to "Zero time" should be a red square (Stop). If it's a green arrow, click it. If it stays orange instead of turning red, EasyGecNG isn't connected to the mini reader: go back to step 1.

4. **Check the driver.** If no COM port works, the SPORTident USB driver may be missing. Install it ([Installing EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/installing/)) and restart the computer. If you have SPORTident Config+, see whether it finds the mini reader; if it doesn't either, it's a driver problem.

5. **Check Java.** EasyGecNG needs Java 8 (see [Installing EasyGecNG](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/installing/)).

### A student gets a sad face

A sad face usually means the student really did skip a checkpoint or go out of order. Often they went to the checkpoint but didn't hold the SI card in the box long enough to get a beep.

1. **Ask them to do the course again.** Remind them how: check in at the Clear box and the Start box, visit the checkpoints in order, hold the SI card in each box until it beeps, and check in at the Finish box. If you have time, download their card in [tabular view](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#tabular-view) to see which checkpoints it recorded.
2. **Check which course EasyGecNG picked.** Sometimes it guesses the wrong course for a student. In tabular view you can see which course it chose and change it by hand.

### Students did the course right, but still get a sad face

If students who you know did the course correctly keep getting a sad face, or the times show the checkpoints out of order:

1. **Check that each box is in the right place.** If two boxes are swapped, students visit them in the wrong order.
2. **Synchronize the boxes.** Each SI box has its own clock, and the clocks drift. When one box's clock is off, EasyGecNG thinks students visited it out of order. Follow [Synchronizing the SI boxes](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/#synchronizing-the-si-boxes). We recommend synchronizing every 3 to 4 weeks anyway.
3. **Test it.** Before you set the checkpoints out, put the boxes side by side and do a course yourself with only a second or two between check-ins. If you get a smiley face, the clocks are close enough.

### The SI boxes don't beep

If a student says a box isn't beeping, they need to clear their SI card at the Clear box, then start again.

If a box doesn't beep for anyone, its battery may be low. See [Checking batteries](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/maintenance/#checking-battery-levels).

### The student forgot a box

Downloading shows a mistake if a student forgot to check in at the Clear, Start or Finish box. Have them clear the card and run the course again. Try these mistakes yourself before class so you recognize them (see [Practice scenarios](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#practice-scenarios)).

### EasyGecNG stops responding

Try these in order:

1. Click the red Stop button, then the green Start button.
2. Check that a COM port is chosen (see [EasyGecNG doesn't read SI cards](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/troubleshooting/#easygecng-doesnt-read-si-cards)).
3. Unplug the mini reader from the USB port and plug it back in.
4. Close EasyGecNG and start it again.
5. Restart the computer.
6. Use a clean course file. If you use the same file for too long, it builds up so much data that EasyGecNG slows down (see [EasyGecNG is slow](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/troubleshooting/#easygecng-is-slow)).
7. Reinstall the latest USB driver from SPORTident.

### EasyGecNG is slow

If EasyGecNG takes a long time to show results, the course file may have grown too big. Each time you save, all the results go into the `.egc` file, and they pile up over many classes. Look at the file's size in File Explorer. The file in this example has grown to almost 3.5 MB.

Start over with a clean course file (see [Clean course files](https://curriculum.navigationgames.org/reference/equipment/electronic-timing/running-easygecng/#clean-course-files)), and click **No** when EasyGecNG asks to save, unless you want to keep the results.

### "Do you want to save the current event?"

EasyGecNG asks this when you close it or open another course file. Click **No**, unless you want to keep the results from this class. Saving every time makes the file grow, and big files slow EasyGecNG down.

### Access denied, or can't save the file

If a message pops up when students download or when you save, partly in French, saying "Erreur d'écriture" (write error) and ending in "(Access is denied)", or EasyGecNG says it can't save the file ("fichier"), the folder holding the `.egc` file is read-only.

To fix it:

1. In File Explorer, go to the folder that holds the `.egc` file. The message shows its location.
2. Right-click the folder and choose **Properties**.
3. Near the bottom, next to **Read-only**, look at the box. If it's checked or filled in, click it until it's empty, then click **OK**.

4. If Windows asks whether to apply the change to all subfolders and files, choose **Apply changes to this folder, subfolders and files** and click **OK**.

### Still stuck?

[Contact Navigation Games](mailto:admin@navigationgames.org) and tell us what you see on the screen. A photo of the screen helps.

## Maintaining the SI Boxes

### Synchronizing the SI boxes

Each SI box has its own clock, and the clocks drift over time. When they drift too far apart, EasyGecNG can tell a student they visited checkpoints out of order when they didn't. Synchronize the boxes every 3 to 4 weeks, and whenever students who did a course right are told they made a mistake.

#### Quick method

This copies the SI-Master's clock to all the other boxes, with no computer:

1. Find the box labeled **SI-Master** (it's also the Clear box).
2. Starting with its display blank, insert the purple **Service/OFF** card 3 times until the display shows **EXT MA** (extended master). This also clears its backup memory.
3. Put the metal coupling stick into the SI-Master. Place the SI-Master flat on top of each other box with the other end of the coupling stick in that box's hole, and wait for the beep. That box is now synchronized.
4. Turn the boxes off with the Service/OFF card to save battery.

[Backwoods Orienteering Klubb has detailed instructions with photos](https://backwoodsok.org/check-and-synchronize-si-boxes).

#### Full method, with SPORTident Config+

This sets the SI-Master's clock from the computer first, then copies it to every box.

**You need:** the Service/OFF card, the coupling stick, the SI-Master (Clear box), the other SI boxes (31 to 40, Start, Finish), the mini reader, and a laptop with [SPORTident Config+](https://www.sportident.com/products.html#software) installed.

1. **Connect the mini reader.** Plug it into a USB port. It beeps twice.
2. **Open SPORTident Config+** from its Desktop shortcut.

3. **Check the device connection.** In the Devices menu, the mini reader should be listed. Click the blue refresh button if it isn't.

4. **Check the connection type.** It should say **Direct**. If it says Remote, click the box to change it.

5. **Click Settings.** Config+ reads and shows the mini reader's settings.

6. **Couple the SI-Master to the mini reader.** Place the SI-Master on top of the mini reader and put the coupling stick through both holes.

7. **Change the connection type to Remote** by clicking the connection box.

8. **Click Settings.** Config+ reads the SI-Master's settings. If you get an error, couple the boxes again and click Retry.
9. **Check the settings.** They should be: Code number 1, Operating mode CLR - Clear, Operating time 00:10:00. Change them if needed.

10. **Click Set time.** The SI-Master beeps once.

11. **Close Config+.** You don't need the computer for the rest.
12. **Take the SI-Master and coupling stick off the mini reader.**
13. **Turn off the SI-Master.** Insert the Service/OFF card until the display is blank.
14. **Lay out all the other boxes:** 31 to 40, Start and Finish.

15. **Set the SI-Master to EXT MA.** With its display blank, insert the Service/OFF card 3 times until the display shows **EXT MA**.

16. **Synchronize each box.** Put the coupling stick in the SI-Master. Place the SI-Master flat on top of a box with the stick in both holes. After a few seconds it beeps, and that box's time is set. If it doesn't beep, line them up again. Repeat for every box.

17. **Turn off all the boxes.** Insert the Service/OFF card into each box until its display is blank. Some boxes need it more than once.

### Checking battery levels

**You need:** the Service/OFF card, the coupling stick, all the SI boxes (31 to 40, Start, Finish, Clear), the mini reader, and a laptop with SPORTident Config+.

1. **Connect the mini reader**, **open Config+**, **check the device connection** and **check that the connection type is Direct**, as in steps 1 to 4 above.
2. **Click Settings.**
3. **Couple a box to the mini reader.** Place the box on top of the mini reader and put the coupling stick through both holes.
4. **Change the connection type to Remote.**
5. **Click Settings.** Config+ reads and shows the box's data.
6. **Check the battery:**
   - **Green:** above 3.2 volts is safe.
   - **Yellow:** between 3.0 and 3.2 volts is in between. The box may still work for another event.
   - **Red:** below 3.0 volts is low. Replace the battery.

7. **Write it down.** We recommend tracking each box's battery level over time.
8. **Turn off the box.** Take it and the coupling stick off the mini reader, and insert the Service/OFF card until the display is blank.
9. **Repeat** steps 3 to 8 for each box.

Batteries usually last at least 5 years. To replace them, send the boxes to SPORTident, or [contact Navigation Games](mailto:admin@navigationgames.org).
